The role will report into our Revenue Operations team. This detail-oriented and highly analytical professional will build and maintain the spreadsheet-based models that power our accounts receivable and invoicing accuracy process. The Business Operations Lead will work hands-on in the data — using complex spreadsheet formulas, pivot tables, and automation tools to identify invoice discrepancies, reconcile billing errors, and ensure accurate, timely collections. While the core focus is on the accuracy and integrity of the underlying data, this role does involve some customer-facing interaction — including light, indirect negotiation to resolve billing discrepancies — along with regular exposure to Location Managers and leadership as part of partnering cross-functionally to resolve issues at the source.

 

This hybrid position is based in the corporate office in Redwood Shores, CA and requires 3 in-office days per week (Monday, Tuesday, Thursday). Only local candidates will be considered.

• Partner directly with the Senior Manager of Revenue Operations to build, test, and refine spreadsheet-based models that support AR aging, invoice accuracy, and collections tracking
  • Own the ongoing maintenance of these models once built, ensuring they remain accurate and reliable as business needs evolve
  • Use complex formulas, pivot tables, and Google Apps Script automation to streamline data processing and reduce manual work
  • Investigate discrepancies between invoiced amounts and underlying contract/pricing data, applying a detail-oriented, investigative approach to root-cause each issue
  • Communicate and collaborate directly with Location Managers and internal stakeholders to resolve billing discrepancies, gathering the context needed to correct and reconcile invoices
  • Contribute to collections efforts throughout the AR lifecycle — not just after discrepancies are resolved — by proactively flagging at-risk accounts, surfacing potential issues early, and supporting outreach in parallel with ongoing discrepancy resolution and model maintenance
  • Adapt invoice formatting and reporting to meet varying customer/district requirements
  • Produce and distribute regular AR aging and reconciliation reports to Revenue Operations leadership
  • Identify recurring sources of invoice error or data discrepancy and recommend process improvements to prevent recurrence
  • Explore and apply AI tools with clear business logic to improve the speed and accuracy of reconciliation and modeling work

• 5+ years of experience in financial/business operations analysis, revenue operations, billing operations, or a related analytical role
  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Finance, Accounting, or a related field preferred
  • Advanced spreadsheet skills required — complex formulas, nested functions, and pivot tables in Excel and/or Google Sheets
  • Familiarity with Google Apps Script automation is a strong plus
  • Comfort using AI tools to support clear, well-defined business logic and workflows
  • Strong foundational understanding of financial and accounting concepts, particularly as they relate to invoicing, billing, and accounts receivable
  • Exceptional attention to detail and a genuine curiosity for finding and resolving discrepancies in data
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills — comfortable working directly with Location Managers and cross-functional stakeholders to resolve issues
  • Highly process-driven, with the discipline to build, document, and maintain repeatable workflows
  • Strong quantitative skills are required, with an emphasis on analytical rigor and attention to detail
  • Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, high-growth environment, managing multiple priorities and deadlines simultaneously
    •  
    The targeted base salary range for this role is listed in the compensation section below. Actual salary may be above or below this range based on factors such as location, skills, and relevant experience. In addition, this position may include additional compensation in the form of equity or commissions. If you are a full-time salaried or hourly worker, we offer the following benefits: Medical, Dental, Vision, 401(k), Holidays, Wellness, Vacation, and more. The targeted pay range for this role in US CA is: $111,000 - $147,000

We’re looking for a Chief of Staff to be a force multiplier for our COO.  You’ll sit at the center of a fast-growing operating business, where new districts, yards, and markets launch while existing ones are still being built out. Your job is to help the COO see around corners: run the operating rhythm, drive the company’s highest-priority cross-functional initiatives, and turn messy operational data into decisions.
You’ll work across Operations, Finance, Sales, HR, Legal, Safety, and Technology, and you’ll have regular exposure across the executive team and Board. You’ll take on the problems that don’t have an owner yet, build the structure around them, and hand them off once they run on their own.
This is a fast-paced environment where the scope changes week to week. If you need a clearly defined lane this one isn’t for you. But if you want to be close to the decisions, enjoy getting into the details of an operating business, and like building things from scratch, keep reading.
This is a hybrid position based out of our headquarters in Redwood City, CA. You will be required to be onsite 3 days per week (Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday). We will only consider candidates already located in the Bay Area.

lists.content:
• Operating Rhythm & Executive Cadence: Own the COO’s operating system: weekly KPI reviews, monthly business reviews, forecast-to-actual reviews, and seasonal planning cycles (back-to-school readiness, budgeting, renewals). Make sure the right data is in the room, decisions get made, and follow-ups actually close.
  • Strategic Initiatives & Special Projects: Lead high-impact, cross-functional projects on the COO’s behalf, such as new market entry, cost and margin improvement programs, process and systems rollouts, and operational turnarounds. Scope the problem, build the plan, drive execution across teams, and report progress.
  • Analysis & Decision Support: Build models and analyses that inform major decisions: unit economics by contract and market, labor cost and margin drivers, capacity and scaling forecasts, pricing and renewal scenarios. Translate complex analysis into clear recommendations.
  • Planning, Budgeting & Performance Management: Partner with Finance on annual planning, budget, and forecasting for the operations organization. Help define KPIs and targets, establish baselines, and hold the business accountable to them.
  • Board & Executive Communications: Prepare operations content for board meetings, investor updates, and executive team reviews. Draft the COO’s communications, talking points, and decision memos, and ensure what goes up the chain is accurate, concise, and defensible.
  • Cross-Functional Alignment: Be the connective tissue between Operations and HQ functions. Anticipate friction, clarify decision rights, and keep leaders aligned on priorities, resources, and timing.
  • Special Requests: Act as a trusted sounding board and extension of the COO. Triage inbound requests, manage the COO’s time and priorities against the company’s biggest bets, and step in on whatever is most urgent.

• 8+ years of experience in management consulting, investment banking, private equity, corporate strategy, or FP&A/strategic finance. Top-tier management consulting experience (McKinsey, BCG, Bain, or equivalent) is a strong plus

  • Advanced financial modeling and analytical skills, comfortable building a P&L or unit economics model from scratch

  • Proven ability to lead complex, cross-functional projects and drive results without direct authority

  • Strong written and verbal communication, including experience preparing materials for senior executives and boards

  • Sound judgment and discretion with confidential information (labor, financial, legal, and personnel matters)

  • Self-starter mentality: you’re comfortable with ambiguity, take initiative, and don’t wait to be told what to do

  • Willingness to get close to the field, including visiting yards and meeting with operators and district partners

  • Experience in operations-heavy, field-based, or asset-intensive industries (transportation, logistics, infrastructure, energy, or similar)

  • Prior experience as a Chief of Staff, or in a business operations or strategy role supporting an operating executive

  • Background in a high-growth, venture- or PE-backed company

  • Familiarity with public sector contracting, labor and union environments, or education-related markets

  • Experience with BI and data tools (SQL, Looker, Tableau, or similar) and comfort working with large operational datasets

  • Bachelor’s degree required; MBA a plus

We’re looking for a Corporate Paralegal & Legal Program Manager to support a lean, fast-moving Legal function and report directly to the General Counsel. You’ll manage corporate compliance activities and coordinate closely with our legal teams, operations and electrification teams, and finance to keep a multi-state, multi-entity company in good standing, and you’ll run projects that help Legal deliver and the business scale: complex transactions, corporate governance, outside counsel and vendor management, legal budget and reporting, and cross-functional initiatives. This is a builder’s role. You’ll bring structure where needed, and you’ll be the go-to person the GC and the business count on to keep things moving.

This is a high-volume, fast-paced environment with a lean team. If you like owning your lane, juggling many workstreams, and making the legal function run better, keep reading.

This role is based at the Company’s headquarters in Redwood Shores, CA and requires you to be onsite 3x/week (Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday). 

Key Responsibilities

Corporate Governance & Entity Management: Maintain the corporate records for Zum and its subsidiaries: minute books, board and stockholder consents and resolutions, cap table support, and corporate level entity controls, signature and delegation policies, and other policy compliance activities. Prepare materials for board and committee meetings. Manage entity formation, qualifications, and track annual filing compliance.

Corporate Finance & Grant Compliance: Support complex corporate finance transactions including debt and equity agreements and related negotiations, know-your-customer and diligence processes. Manage closing checklists and signature page logistics for financings.Track compliance with credit agreement and investor-agreement obligations: compliance certificates, financial reporting deliverables, notice requirements, covenant calendars, and consent and approval rights.

Government Relations Support.Track lobbying registrations, periodic lobbying reports, political contribution and gift/ethics compliance, and trade association memberships.

Legal Program & Project Management: Own the Legal team’s project roadmap. Run cross-functional initiatives from kickoff through completion, such as policy rollouts, contract and records refreshes, diligence and audit responses, and new-market or new-entity launches. Set priorities with the GC, track deliverables, and report status.

Outside Counsel & Vendor Management: Manage the outside counsel roster, engagement letters, and rate arrangements. Review invoices against budgets and billing guidelines, track spend by matter and function, and prepare regular legal spend reports for the GC and Finance. Manage legal vendors and subscriptions (e.g., Harvey, e-signature, registered agent, research tools).

Process Improvement: Document and improve Legal’s internal workflows. Build checklists, templates, and dashboards. Identify where automation and AI tools (e.g., Harvey) can remove manual work, and support Legal's AI governance, including vendor evaluation, data handling review, and usage guidelines for tools like Harvey. 

Department Administration: Manage the Legal budget tracking, department metrics, the knowledge base and self-service resources for the business.

Required Qualifications

  • 5+ years of experience as a corporate paralegal or similar role  in a law firm or in-house.  
  • Hands-on experience with corporate governance and entity management (minute books, consents, Secretary of State filings, multi-state qualifications)
  • Experience with debt or equity financings from the paralegal side (closing checklists, officer's certificates, UCC/lien searches, consents).
  • Demonstrated ability to exercise judgment on routine matters and escalate appropriately to the GC or inhouse attorneys.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines at once with minimal oversight
  • Experience managing outside counsel relationships and reviewing or tracking legal invoices and budgets
  • Strong written communication and attention to detail; able to produce clean, board-ready work product
  • Self-starter who is comfortable with ambiguity and builds structure where none exists
  • Bachelor’s degree required; paralegal certificate or equivalent training a plus
  • Comfort handling highly confidential, material nonpublic information.
  • Strong Excel/spreadsheet and dashboard skills for spend, deadline, and obligation tracking.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with entity management and matter management tools (e.g., Boardvantage, Unity or similar)
  • Familiarity with CLM platforms (Linksquares a plus) and e-signature tools
  • Experience implementing AI-enabled legal tools
  • PMP or other project management certification, or a track record of running complex cross-functional projects
  • Background in a high-growth technology company, or in transportation, education, or public-sector environments
  • Experience supporting a venture-backed company through financings and board reporting

The targeted base salary range for this role is listed in the compensation section below. Actual salary may be above or below this range based on factors such as location, skills, and relevant experience. In addition, this position may include additional compensation in the form of equity or commissions. If you are a full-time salaried or hourly worker, we offer the following benefits: Medical, Dental, Vision, 401(k), Holidays, Wellness, Vacation, and more. The targeted pay range for this role in CA, USA is: $150,000 - $175,000 plus stock options.

lists.content:
Zūm provides safe, reliable, technology-enabled student transportation for school districts. As we launch new districts and deepen existing partnerships, we’re hiring a Customer Experience Manager to own the district relationship once the contract is signed.

You’ll be the day-to-day partner for transportation directors and district leaders in your region. That means working side by side with Operations to deliver on our commitments, staying on every issue until the district confirms it’s resolved, and presenting results to district leadership and boards. You’ll also spot risk early and lead renewal conversations. This is a hands-on role for someone who is organized, responsive, and just as comfortable in the district office as in the yard.

• District partnership: Serve as the day-to-day point of contact for assigned districts, building trusted relationships with transportation directors and district staff.
  • Presentations and reporting: Build and deliver business reviews, launch decks, and board or leadership presentations that clearly communicate performance, progress, and next steps.
  • Execution with Operations: Partner daily with regional Operations and yard leaders to turn district requests and commitments into action and confirm they are completed.
  • Direct follow-up: Own communication back to districts on open issues, service concerns, and requests, with clear timelines, status updates, and closure.
  • Escalations: Identify service gaps early, document them, and route them to Operations, Technology, or Finance. Keep the VP informed on high-risk accounts.
  • Retention: Monitor account health and sentiment, flag churn risk early, and carry out account plans set with the VP.
  • Renewals and growth: Prepare renewal materials and support Ops and Sales on rebids, renewals, and expansion opportunities.
  • Onboarding: Coordinate launch activities for new districts, including readiness checklists, dry runs, and district and family communications.
  • Technology adoption: Train and support district staff and families on the Zūm CMX platform and drive usage.
  • Metrics and reporting: Track health scores and KPIs, including on-time performance, response times, and sentiment, and turn them into weekly action.
  • Voice of customer: Capture district feedback and share recurring themes with Product, Technology, and Operations.

• First 30 days: Learn the product, shadow handoffs, and meet your assigned districts and regional Ops leads.
  • First 90 days: Establish strong rapport as district thought partner, run kickoffs or take over existing accounts, with a success plan in place for each district.
  • First year: Hit retention and renewal targets, improve on-time performance and response metrics in your region, and contribute to the CS playbook.

• 5+ years in customer experience/success, account management, or district-level roles in student transportation, logistics, SaaS, or a similar service-critical field.
  • Strong presentation skills, with experience building and delivering executive-ready materials to district leaders or boards.
  • Proven ability to coordinate with operations teams and drive cross-functional work to completion.
  • Exceptional organization and follow-through, with the ability to manage multiple districts and deadlines at once.
  • Fluency with customer data, turned into weekly action.
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication.
  • Willingness to travel up to 80% within the region.
  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience.

About the Role 
We're seeking a skilled Technician II to contribute to maintenance operations at our San Bernardino, CA site. This role encompasses vehicle diagnostics, repairs, and preventive maintenance with increasing complexity. You'll diagnose mechanical and electrical issues, assist with major component rebuilds, and ensure vehicles meet stringent safety and compliance standards. You'll be a vital part of our transportation operations, maintaining fleet reliability and safety for students and communities.
 
 
What Makes You Successful in This Role 
You're a developing technician who excels in a dynamic maintenance environment where challenges vary daily. You balance efficiency with meticulous attention to safety and quality standards. You're a capable problem-solver who can diagnose issues across major vehicle systems and execute repairs with confidence. You're eager to expand your skills and learn from senior technicians while taking ownership of your assigned work. You're comfortable performing diagnostics with modern tools, executing complex electrical and AC repairs, and maintaining thorough documentation. You keep your workspace organized, follow proper procedures, and consistently deliver quality repairs.
 
Responsibilities 
Vehicle Diagnostics & Repair 
● Diagnose malfunctions and perform vehicle repairs including steering, electrical, cooling, lubricating, braking systems, drive trains, suspensions, power steering units, clutches, transmissions, and oil, temperature, gas regulating components, and related assigned duties within qualification level, in accordance with all relevant Federal, State/Provincial and local guidelines and requirements
● Assist Tech I’s with the rebuilding of engines, transmissions, and differentials as assigned by the manager
● Perform test drives during Preventative Maintenance inspections to identify driver reported issues and conduct test drives after service to confirm repairs have been completed successfully
 
Maintenance Operations & Quality Control 
● Arrange for and obtain appropriate inspections and approval of all major repairs before the vehicle is released from the maintenance facility
● Identify and report any additional maintenance and/or repairs found necessary in conducting assigned repairs and maintenance including repairs and maintenance required to be performed by Technicians with a higher qualification level
● Perform work assigned by manager or lead when supervised
● Record time spent, parts used and repairs and/or maintenance conducted on the appropriate form
● Perform road calls and on-the-road repairs as assigned
 
Safety & Compliance 
● Maintain a safe, clean, productive, and efficient work area including ensuring the work area is in compliance with all relevant Federal, State/Provincial, local guidelines and requirements, and company Housekeeping standards and safety regulations
● Advise Lead Technician of unsafe maintenance conditions or practices and/or vehicle abuse
● Work assigned shift and overtime as needed (AM/PM)
 
Qualifications 
Basic Qualifications: 
● Minimum of two to four years medium/heavy truck Fleet mechanic repair experience
● Diagnostic, Electrical, and AC skills are a must
● Technical knowledge of major vehicle systems and diesel equipment is required
● Previous fleet experience with familiarity with diesel and gasoline systems
● Possess the recommended minimum hand tools for a Medium and Heavy Duty and Diesel Technician
● Ability to use good judgment and decision-making skills
● Valid CDL License (Must be able to obtain within the first 90 days of employment)
● ASE Certification in brakes, suspension, engine, electrical, A/C or a Master School Bus and/or a Master Truck Technician

**This role is primarily remote, with an expectation that candidates are located within close proximity to a Zum yard.**

As a Director of Driver (supply) Growth, you will be responsible for supporting the driver planning and hiring results (CDL, non-CDL drivers, and bus attendants) for all Zūm yard locations. This role will be responsible for partnering with multiple stakeholders to forecast staffing driver needs and training/onboarding resource needs for peak (back to school) and non-peak timeframe. You will also be working with the local safety and training teams to standardize as well as maximize the training and certification process, and enhancing the driver onboarding experience. This role requires exceptional communication and interpersonal skills with Operations, Finance, Recruiting, and HR stakeholders in a high-pressure environment. You will manage a high-visibility and large scale program, and partner with all levels of leadership to exercise sound judgment where clear guidelines may not exist.

lists.content:
• Strategic Leadership: Develop and implement a comprehensive strategy for scaling and managing the entire driver acquisition process. Provide visionary leadership to ensure the growth and success of our driver base.

  • Forecasting and Budget Oversight: Ensure accurate projection of driver forecasts and manage hiring campaigns within allocated budgets. Implement cost-effective strategies and monitor performance against financial goals.

  • End-to-End Process Ownership: Oversee the complete lifecycle of driver acquisition, from recruitment to onboarding. Implement processes to ensure drivers are properly vetted, credentialed, and trained/onboard according to Zum's standards.

  • Performance Metrics and Visibility: Own driver recruiting performance metrics, developing and tracking key performance indicators (KPIs) to measure the success of driver growth initiatives. Provide regular visibility and reports to the leadership team.

  • Competitor Analysis: Conduct competitive analysis both at the national and market level from the driver acquisitions point of view. Implement best practices to maintain a competitive edge in driver recruitment and retention and set Zum apart from competition- making Zum the most desirable employer for school bus drivers in the world.

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Collaborate with cross-functional teams to align driver growth strategies with overall company objectives. Foster strong partnerships with other departments to enhance overall operational efficiency and reduce acquisition costs.

• Master's degree in statistics, HR, mathematics, economics, or MBA.

  • 10+ years of domain experience including experience leading a workforce planning team that works across partner sub teams. Familiarity solving problems/efforts with visible and not-yet-visible risks, roadblocks, constraints, including many that conflict with each other.

  • Experience supporting and influencing senior executives.

  • Experience setting technical requirements for process automation.

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, expertise in deriving insights through data analysis, and practical knowledge and experience in inferential statistical application.

  • Excellent attention to detail and the ability to dive deep into the data.

  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills, including the ability to engage effectively with a broad range of audiences including senior business leaders and cross-functional colleagues.

  • Ability to work efficiently in a dynamic and ambiguous environment by combining analytical rigor and judgment.

lists.content:
Daily Operations & Route Management
  • Direct and monitor daily assignments, schedule drivers, and assign vehicles to ensure full route coverage and on-time completion of all driver activities.
  • Communicate all relevant details of driving assignments to drivers to ensure proper execution, and assist with routing directions and special service assignments.
  • Coordinate vehicle service and repairs with the Maintenance Manager to ensure uninterrupted service delivery.
    • Communication & Emergency Response
  • Respond to emergency calls and coordinate the emergency response network.
  • Notify stakeholders and location personnel of all route changes, emergencies, accidents, breakdowns, or service disruptions, and handle customer concerns promptly and professionally.
  • Provide real-time operational support to drivers including assistance with traffic issues, routing questions, and emergency situations, escalating unresolved issues appropriately.
    • Compliance & Administrative Operations
  • Maintain route documentation and records including contracts, customer information, route changes, maps, vehicle assignments, and driver details to ensure accuracy and compliance with district and state requirements.
  • Ensure strict adherence to dispatch standard operating procedures and recommend disciplinary action for policy violations in coordination with management.
  • Track and document operational activities, incidents, and communications for reporting purposes while partnering with Location Manager and Safety Manager on compliance objectives.
    •

Basic Qualifications:
  • High school diploma or equivalentProficiency with Microsoft or G Suite applications (Sheets, Docs, Slides, etc.).
  • Experience in high-pressure, time-sensitive operations (e.g., transportation, logistics, field services, customer service, hospitality, or similar fast-paced environments).
    • Preferred Qualifications:
  • Background in a leadership, supervisory, or management capacity within fast-paced operational environments.
  • Previous school busing or transportation experience, either as a driver or dispatcher is a plus.
  • Knowledge of state DOT/DMV safety rules and company compliance expectations.
  • Excellent oral and written communication skills with strong interpersonal abilitiesExperience working in a union environment.
  • Comprehensive knowledge of the local area, including traffic patterns, road restrictions, neighborhoods, and geography of the school district is highly desirableStrong organizational, prioritization, and time management skills with demonstrated ability to manage multiple tasks simultaneously, coordinate scheduling and task assignments, maintain accurate records and filing systems, and track assets and inventory.

About the Role
We're seeking an experienced Field Supervisor to provide on-the-ground safety oversight and operational support for our transportation team. This role is the eyes and ears in the field, ensuring safe, compliant, and efficient operation of all district transportation routes through direct observation, driver coaching, and real-time incident response. You'll spend your days riding routes, conducting safety audits, supporting drivers, and responding to emergencies—all while maintaining the highest safety standards and building a culture of excellence. You'll be the trusted leader drivers turn to for guidance and the safety champion who ensures every student arrives safely, every time.
What Makes You Successful in This Role
You're a safety-minded leader who loves being out in the field rather than behind a desk. You're naturally observant, catching safety issues before they become problems, and you know how to coach drivers in a way that's direct but respectful. You stay calm under pressure—whether you're responding to an accident scene, helping a new driver navigate a tricky route, or addressing a parent’s concern. You genuinely care about driver success and student safety, and you're not afraid to have tough conversations when needed. You're comfortable juggling route observations, incident investigations, documentation, and training support—all in the same day. You bring a steady, approachable presence that earns respect from drivers and builds confidence with schools and families.
Responsibilities
Route Oversight & Safety Compliance
Conduct daily ride-alongs, route observations, and stop audits (AM/PM) to ensure safe and compliant operations while monitoring on-time performance and identifying operational inefficiencies
Verify drivers follow proper student loading/unloading procedures in adherence to federal, state, and district transportation regulations
Perform random DOT compliance checks, verify documentation, inspect pre-trip/post-trip procedures and vehicle cleanliness, and monitor proper use of seat belts, student management procedures, and emergency evacuation readiness
Driver Support, Coaching & Training
Provide on-the-spot coaching and immediate written feedback when safety violations or procedural concerns arise, and follow up on performance metrics or operational issues
Support new drivers with route-specific training, shadowing, and monitored practice drives while serving as first point of contact for guidance, conflict resolution, and real-time operational support
Conduct informal reviews of safe-driving techniques and behavior-management strategies, and support or facilitate safety meetings, refresher trainings, annual recertifications, and track employee compliance for required certifications
Incident Response & Operational Support
Respond immediately to road calls, breakdowns, and accidents to ensure student safety, assist drivers, and conduct post-incident checks
Complete initial incident reports, gather necessary information for Safety and Operations teams, and ensure timely communication to school districts and company leadership during safety-related events
Document observations, coaching notes, and performance issues in required systems, and monitor yard operations to ensure buses are ready, fueled, and staged properly for routes
Qualifications
Basic Qualifications
Possession of a Commercial Driver's License (CDL) Class B with Passenger (P) and School Bus (S) endorsements and current DOT Medical Certificate
Minimum of two (2) years of relevant industry experience in Safety Department operations, school bus operations, or dispatch
Knowledge of local and state laws and regulations pertaining to the school bus industry and District policies
Preferred Qualifications
Demonstrated knowledge of school bus safety regulations and best practices
Basic computer proficiency with G-Suite applications (Sheets, Docs, Slides)
Proven record of leading teams and implementing new safety programs and initiatives
Proficiency with reporting and safety tools including incident reports, Gatekeeper, Netradyne, and camera systems, etc.
Experience investigating accidents and incidents with completion of all required documentation and reporting
Familiarity with accident reporting

descriptionBody:
About the Role

We're seeking an experienced Field Supervisor to provide on-the-ground safety oversight and operational support for our transportation team. This role is the eyes and ears in the field, ensuring safe, compliant, and efficient operation of all district transportation routes through direct observation, driver coaching, and real-time incident response. You'll spend your days riding routes, conducting safety audits, supporting drivers, and responding to emergencies—all while maintaining the highest safety standards and building a culture of excellence. You'll be the trusted leader drivers turn to for guidance and the safety champion who ensures every student arrives safely, every time.

What Makes You Successful in This Role

You're a safety-minded leader who loves being out in the field rather than behind a desk. You're naturally observant, catching safety issues before they become problems, and you know how to coach drivers in a way that's direct but respectful. You stay calm under pressure—whether you're responding to an accident scene, helping a new driver navigate a tricky route, or addressing a parent’s concern. You genuinely care about driver success and student safety, and you're not afraid to have tough conversations when needed. You're comfortable juggling route observations, incident investigations, documentation, and training support—all in the same day. You bring a steady, approachable presence that earns respect from drivers and builds confidence with schools and families.

Responsibilities

Route Oversight & Safety Compliance

  • Conduct daily ride-alongs, route observations, and stop audits (AM/PM) to ensure safe and compliant operations while monitoring on-time performance and identifying operational inefficiencies

  • Verify drivers follow proper student loading/unloading procedures in adherence to federal, state, and district transportation regulations

  • Perform random DOT compliance checks, verify documentation, inspect pre-trip/post-trip procedures and vehicle cleanliness, and monitor proper use of seat belts, student management procedures, and emergency evacuation readiness

Driver Support, Coaching & Training

  • Provide on-the-spot coaching and immediate written feedback when safety violations or procedural concerns arise, and follow up on performance metrics or operational issues

  • Support new drivers with route-specific training, shadowing, and monitored practice drives while serving as first point of contact for guidance, conflict resolution, and real-time operational support

  • Conduct informal reviews of safe-driving techniques and behavior-management strategies, and support or facilitate safety meetings, refresher trainings, annual recertifications, and track employee compliance for required certifications

Incident Response & Operational Support

  • Respond immediately to road calls, breakdowns, and accidents to ensure student safety, assist drivers, and conduct post-incident checks

  • Complete initial incident reports, gather necessary information for Safety and Operations teams, and ensure timely communication to school districts and company leadership during safety-related events

  • Document observations, coaching notes, and performance issues in required systems, and monitor yard operations to ensure buses are ready, fueled, and staged properly for routes

Qualifications

Basic Qualifications

  • Possession of a Commercial Driver's License (CDL) Class B with Passenger (P) and School Bus (S) endorsements and current DOT Medical Certificate

  • Minimum of two (2) years of relevant industry experience in Safety Department operations, school bus operations, or dispatch

  • Knowledge of local and state laws and regulations pertaining to the school bus industry and District policies

Preferred Qualifications

  • Demonstrated knowledge of school bus safety regulations and best practices

  • Basic computer proficiency with G-Suite applications (Sheets, Docs, Slides)

  • Proven record of leading teams and implementing new safety programs and initiatives

  • Proficiency with reporting and safety tools including incident reports, Gatekeeper, Netradyne, and camera systems, etc.

  • Experience investigating accidents and incidents with completion of all required documentation and reporting

  • Familiarity with accident reporting

I read "language" as the English proficiency requirement plus the bilingual preference. Board and exit buses repeatedly throughout the shift, climb steps, and kneel, crouch, or crawl to inspect under seats and beneath vehicles
Lift, carry, or assist with up to 50 pounds, including helping students during emergency evacuations and evacuation drills
Sit for long periods in a moving vehicle, and stand or walk for long periods in the yard and at bus stops
Work Environment & Schedule
Respond on short notice to breakdowns and accident scenes, including roadside locations near active traffic
Work outdoors in all weather conditions, including heat, cold, rain, and low light
Work a split shift with early morning starts (as early as [5:00 a.m.]) and afternoon routes, plus on-call coverage for road calls as scheduled
Use mobile devices, camera systems, and Zūm's CMX platform to monitor routes and document observations in the field

Write clear, factual incident reports, coaching notes, and observation records
Safety-Sensitive Position

Consent to a full pre-employment query and annual queries of the FMCSA Drug & Alcohol Clearinghouse
Keep a valid CDL with required endorsements, a current DOT Medical Certificate, and the state school bus certification for their assigned yard (California School Bus Driver Certificate or Washington OSPI School Bus Driver Authorization)
Clear a criminal background check, including fingerprint clearance required for working with students, and keep a motor vehicle record that meets Zūm's standards, reviewed before hire and at least once a year
Report any license suspension, citation, or change in medical status to the company right away, as required by federal and state regulations

Conduct daily ride-alongs, route observations, and stop audits (AM/PM) to ensure safe and compliant operations while monitoring on-time performance and identifying operational inefficiencies
Verify drivers follow proper student loading/unloading procedures in adherence to federal, state, and school district transportation regulations
Perform random DOT compliance checks, verify documentation, inspect pre-trip/post-trip procedures and vehicle cleanliness, and monitor proper use of seat belts, student management procedures, and emergency evacuation readiness
Driver Support, Coaching & Training
Provide on-the-spot coaching and immediate written feedback when safety violations or procedural concerns arise, and follow up on performance metrics or operational issues
Support new drivers with route-specific training, shadowing, and monitored practice drives while serving as first point of contact for guidance, conflict resolution, and real-time operational support
Conduct informal reviews of safe-driving techniques and behavior-management strategies, and support or facilitate safety meetings, refresher trainings, annual recertifications, and track employee compliance for required certifications
Incident Response & Operational Support
Respond immediately to road calls, breakdowns, and accidents to ensure student safety, assist drivers, and conduct post-incident checks
Complete initial incident reports, gather necessary information for Safety and Operations teams, and ensure timely communication to school districts and company leadership during safety-related events
Document observations, coaching notes, and performance issues in required systems, and monitor yard operations to ensure buses are ready, fueled, and staged properly for routes
Qualifications
Basic Qualifications
Possession of a Commercial Driver's License (CDL) Class A or B with Passenger (P) and School Bus Driver (S) endorsements and current DOT Medical Certificate
Minimum of two (2) years of relevant industry experience in Safety Department operations, school bus operations, or dispatch
Knowledge of local and state laws and regulations pertaining to the school bus industry and District policies (or learn within 60 days)
Preferred Qualifications
Demonstrated knowledge of school bus safety regulations and best practices
CHP-certified School Bus Driver Instructor credential preferred (or ability to attain within 6 months)
Basic computer proficiency with Google Workspace-Suite applications (Sheets, Docs, Slides)
Proven record of leading teams and implementing new safety programs and initiatives
Proficiency with reporting and safety tools including incident reports, Gatekeeper, Netradyne, and camera systems, etc.
Experience investigating accidents and incidents with completion of all required documentation and reporting
Familiarity with accident reporting
 
I read "language" as the English proficiency requirement plus the bilingual preference. That matters more than usual right now because FMCSA is enforcing English proficiency as an out-of-service violation for CDL holders. The 50-lb lift is a placeholder, so match it to whatever your driver JD uses.
 

 
Essential Functions & Working Conditions
The essential functions of this role include the physical and environmental demands below. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform these functions.
Physical Demands
Safely operate a school bus during ride-alongs, route coverage, and training drives, and meet FMCSA physical qualification standards for commercial drivers (49 CFR 391.41)
Board and exit buses repeatedly throughout the shift, climb steps, and kneel, crouch, or crawl to inspect under seats and beneath vehicles
Lift, carry, or assist with up to 50 pounds, including helping students during emergency evacuations and evacuation drills
Sit for long periods in a moving vehicle, and stand or walk for long periods in the yard and at bus stops
Work Environment & Schedule
Respond on short notice to breakdowns and accident scenes, including roadside locations near active traffic
Work outdoors in all weather conditions, including heat, cold, rain, and low light
Work a split shift with early morning starts (as early as [5:00 a.m.]) and afternoon routes, plus on-call coverage for road calls as scheduled
Use mobile devices, camera systems, and Zūm's CMX platform to monitor routes and document observations in the field
Language Requirements
Read and speak English well enough to talk with the public, understand highway traffic signs and signals, respond to official questions from law enforcement and inspectors, and complete reports and records, as required of all commercial drivers under 49 CFR 391.11(b)(2)
Communicate clearly and calmly with students, parents, school staff, and emergency responders, including during active incidents
Write clear, factual incident reports, coaching notes, and observation records
Safety-Sensitive Position
This is a safety-sensitive position under U.S. Department of Transportation and FMCSA regulations (49 CFR Part 382). As a condition of hire and continued employment, the Field Supervisor must:
Pass a pre-employment drug test and take part in random, post-accident, reasonable suspicion, return-to-duty, and follow-up drug and alcohol testing
Consent to a full pre-employment query and annual queries of the FMCSA Drug & Alcohol Clearinghouse
Keep a valid CDL with required endorsements, a current DOT Medical Certificate, and the state school bus certification for their assigned yard (California School Bus Driver Certificate or Washington OSPI School Bus Driver Authorization)
Clear a criminal background check, including fingerprint clearance required for working with students, and keep a motor vehicle record that meets Zūm's standards, reviewed before hire and at least once a year
Report any license suspension, citation, or change in medical status to the company right away, as required by federal and state regulations

About Zūm:

About the Role:
We're seeking an experienced Location Manager to lead transportation operations in Shawnee, KS. This role encompasses the complete operational lifecycle—from bid development and startup to daily management and continuous improvement. You'll build high-performing teams, manage P&L accountability, and establish best-in-class transportation operations that exceed customer expectations. 
 
What Makes You Successful in This Role: 
You're a decisive leader who thrives in dynamic, fast-paced environments where every day brings new challenges. You balance operational urgency with safety discipline, never compromising on what matters most. You're a natural relationship builder who earns trust with customers, employees, and stakeholders through consistent follow-through. You see potential in people and invest in their growth, building teams that take ownership and deliver results. You're equally comfortable reviewing financial reports, walking the yard with drivers, and presenting to school district administrators. You take pride in building something from the ground up and have the resilience and initiative to overcome obstacles without waiting for permission. 
 
Responsibilities: 
Operational Leadership & Start-Up 
● Execute complete site start-ups for newly awarded contracts, team hiring, facility setup, IT implementation 
● Develop training and hiring programs for location that meets or exceeds state, federal, and district guidelines 
● Develop and maintain customer and stakeholder relationships, consistently exceeding expectations through proactive communication and service delivery 
● Manage assigned contract operations, ensuring consistency and excellence 
 
Performance Management & Safety 
● Utilize Zum's IT infrastructure to monitor, analyze, and exceed balanced scorecard KPIs across all operational areas 
● Spearhead a behavioral safety culture that protects employees, students, and the broader community 
● Oversee Safety Department compliance with state, federal, DOT regulations, RFP requirements, and meticulous record keeping 
● Review all incident reports, ensure proper accident/incident reporting procedures, and submit documentation as required 
● Maintain P&L accountability in alignment with company financial guidelines 
 
Team Development & Operations 
● Collaborate with Human Resources, Recruiting, and Safety teams to strategize and execute hiring plans that support operational needs 
● Develop and coach Zum employees to become our next generation of leaders through mentoring and growth opportunities 
● Partner with Maintenance leaders to ensure complete fleet readiness and maintain accurate inventory meeting all regulatory and contractual requirements 
● Oversee daily operations including scheduling, staffing, field trip/charter processes, route awards, and trip execution 
● Work with the payroll department to ensure timely, accurate processing and resolve discrepancies promptly 
● Manage union relationship according to the collective bargaining agreement (CBA) guidelines 
● Maintain organized, safe, clean, and efficient operational facilities 
● Partner with Safety Manager to coordinate accident investigations and workers' compensation cases, working with insurance adjusters and claims administrators to ensure accountability and timely resolution 
● Build and maintain strong relationships with school district partners and community to ensure service excellence 
 
Electrification Project Management 
● Plan, execute, and complete school bus yard electrification projects on time, within budget, and to specification 
● Manage project plans, schedules, budgets, and coordinate with contractors, school district staff, utilities, and AHJs 
● Monitor progress, report on status, risks, and issues, and resolve project-related conflicts 
● Ensure compliance with safety regulations and environmental standards throughout project lifecycle 
 
QUALIFICATIONS: 
Basic Qualifications 
● Demonstrated experience managing full profit and loss (P&L) accountability with operational oversight and KPI responsibility 
● 5+ years of experience managing day-to-day operations in complex, time-sensitive environments such as transportation, field services, logistics, hospitality, or similar industries 
● Experience with scheduling, staffing, planning, and operational execution 
● 5+ years of experience maintaining client-facing relationships and managing customer accounts in an operational environment, with demonstrated ability to deliver customer service to both external clients and internal stakeholders 
● Experience managing salaried leaders and/or coordinating across multiple departments 
● Track record of career progression supported by relevant certifications or continuing education, with demonstrated success in developing direct reports and building high-performing teams 
● Comprehensive understanding of and demonstrated experience with safety practices, protocols, processes, compliance requirements, and regulatory standards 
 
Preferred Qualifications 
● Experience managing in a unionized (CBA) environment 
● Prior leadership in transportation start-up or new district launch, including sourcing facilities, implementing IT systems, building teams, and intaking fleet vehicles 
● Demonstrated experience successfully managing through periods of rapid organizational growth or major management/structural changes 
● Proficiency with Microsoft or G Suite applications (Sheets, Docs, Slides)
 
The targeted base salary range for this role is listed in the compensation section below. Actual salary may be above or below this range based on factors such as location, skills, and relevant experience. In addition, this position may include additional compensation in the form of bonus, equity, or commissions. If you are a full-time salaried or hourly worker, we offer the following benefits: Medical, Dental, Vision, 401(k), Holidays, Wellness, Vacation, and more. 
The targeted pay range for this role in is: $125,000 - $145,000

About the Role
We're seeking an experienced Operations Supervisor to support daily transportation operations at our Yonker, NY location. Reporting directly to the Location Manager, you'll oversee front-line supervisory teams, ensure operational excellence, and drive performance across all key operational areas. This role is critical to maintaining service quality, team development, and customer satisfaction while supporting the location's strategic goals and growth initiatives.
 
What Makes You Successful in This Role
You're a hands-on leader who thrives in the controlled chaos of daily operations. You know how to balance competing priorities without losing sight of safety, service quality, and team morale. You're a problem-solver who takes ownership and finds solutions rather than excuses. You build trust with your team through consistency, fairness, and genuine investment in their success. You're comfortable working in the field, whether coaching a supervisor through a tough conversation, troubleshooting a route issue, or jumping in to support operations when needed. You communicate clearly up, down, and across the organization, keeping everyone informed and aligned. You understand that operational excellence comes from empowering your team rather than micromanaging them, and you take pride in seeing your people grow and succeed.
 
Responsibilities
Operational Excellence & Performance Management
 • Oversee day-to-day transportation operations, including scheduling, staffing, route assignments, and field trip/charter coordination
 • Monitor and analyze operational KPIs using Zum's IT infrastructure, implementing corrective actions to exceed performance targets
 • Partner with the Location Manager to maintain operational readiness, respond to real-time challenges, and ensure facilities are organized, safe, and efficiently operated
 • Collaborate with the Maintenance Manager to ensure fleet readiness and regulatory compliance while supporting budget management through monitoring of labor costs and operational expenses
Team Leadership & Development
• Directly supervise and coach the staff, providing guidance, feedback, and professional development
• Collaborate with HR, Recruiting, and Safety teams to execute hiring plans,maintain adequate staffing levels, and investigate and resolve employee concerns
• Build a culture of accountability, ownership, and continuous improvement by conducting regular one-on-ones, performance reviews, and development planning with direct reports
• Identify and develop high-potential team members for advancement opportunities
Safety, Compliance & Customer Service
• Champion a behavioral safety culture that prioritizes the well-being of employees, students, and the community while ensuring compliance with all state, federal, DOT regulations, company policies, and customer contract requirements
• Review incident reports, oversee accident/incident reporting procedures, and maintain accurate documentation
• Maintain strong relationships with internal and external customers, ensuring service expectations are consistently met or exceeded
• Respond promptly to customer inquiries, service issues, and operational concerns with professionalism and urgency while acting as an escalation point for problem resolution
 
Qualifications
Basic Qualifications
• 2+ years of experience maintaining client relationships and managing accounts in an operational setting
• 2+ years of supervisory or people-leadership experience managing teams of 25+ employees in fast-paced, time-sensitive operational settings (e.g., transportation, field services, logistics, hospitality, or similar industries)
• 2+ years of experience managing day-to-day operations in complex, time-sensitive environments such as transportation, field services, logistics, hospitality, or similar industries
Preferred
• Bachelor's degree in Business Analytics, Business Management, Operations Management, or related field, or 4+ years of equivalent professional experience in operations leadership
• Experience in a unionized environment and familiarity with collective bargaining agreements (CBAs)
• Experience in K-12 transportation or working with school district customers
Proficiency with transportation management systems, fleet management software, or operational IT platforms, and Microsoft or G Suite applications (Sheets, Docs, Slides, etc.)
• Exceptional organizational skills with the ability to effectively manage concurrent priorities and deadlines
• Demonstrated track record of developing direct reports and building high-performing supervisory teams
• Strong communication and interpersonal skills with the ability to influence and collaborate across all levels of the organization
 
The targeted base salary range for this role is listed in the compensation section below. Actual salary may be above or below this range based on factors such as location, skills, and relevant experience. In addition, this position may include additional compensation in the form of bonus, equity, or commissions. If you are a full-time salaried or hourly worker, we offer the following benefits: Medical, Dental, Vision, 401(k), Holidays, Wellness, Vacation, and more. 
 
The targeted pay range for this role in is: $90,000 - $105,000

lists.content: This role is about relationships, not cold outreach. We're looking for a seasoned business development and/or partnerships professional with experience in K-12 school districts, who is already known, and knows K-12 School District Leaders, including but not limited to Superintendents, Chief Financial Officers (CFOs), Chief Operating Officers (COOs), Business Officials, and Transportation Directors in IL and the Midwest and NY and the Northeast),who shape student mobility decisions. You’ve spent time building relationships in the room with these stakeholders: at conferences, over dinner, on the phone at odd hours. You understand the rhythm of public-sector budget cycles and RFPs, and you know how to move a relationship from a handshake to a signed contract without coming across as transactional. You'll be on Zūm's front lines - building the pipeline, shaping the strategy, and earning business that lets Zūm reach more students.

• Lead new-business growth for Zūm across a defined state or regional territory (e.g., New York or Illinois), building and executing a strategic account and government-relations plan

  • Build and personally maintain deep, durable relationships with Superintendents, district Transportation Directors, Business/Finance Officials, and state-level transportation or education officials

  • Represent Zūm in person — conferences, association events, district visits, and relationship-building engagements (dinners, site visits, industry functions) 

  • Identify and qualify new business opportunities by tracking district budget cycles, contract expirations, RFP calendars, and state policy or funding shifts that create openings

  • Support competitive public-sector RFP processes, assembling and coaching internal teams through written responses and oral/interview presentations

  • Serve as the trusted advisor and go-to relationship for named accounts even after close, ensuring smooth handoff to Operations and protecting the relationship through renewal

  • Represent Zūm with state pupil transportation associations, school board associations, and relevant government affairs forums to build brand presence and credibility

• 10+ years of partnerships, business development, sales, or government relations experience in student transportation, transit, or a closely related public-sector-facing industry

  • Existing, active relationships with Superintendents, COOs, CFO / CBOs, Transportation Directors, and/or state transportation or education officials— this is a relationship-first hire, not a cold-start territory builder

  • Demonstrated success managing long, multi-stakeholder public-sector sales cycles and competitive government RFP processes, including oral/interview presentations

  • Strong consultative selling skills: ability to diagnose a district's pressures and position Zūm CMX credibly 

  • High degree of personal integrity and discretion. This role represents Zūm to public officials and must navigate procurement ethics rules and gift/hospitality policies correctly

  • Existing membership or active involvement in state pupil transportation associations (e.g., TAPT in Texas, NYAPT in New York) or national bodies (NAPT, NSTA)

  • Bachelor's degree, though relevant relationship depth and track record will outweigh formal education requirements

lists.content:
• Process payroll for 1000 + hourly and salaried employees, including adjustments, Bonus, Reimbursement, corrections, retroactive pay and off cycle / manual checks.

  • Administer union payroll per CBA terms, including shift differentials, overtime, and union dues deductions.

  • Review payroll data for accuracy, ensuring proper calculations of wages, taxes, and deductions.

  • Maintain compliance with federal, state, and local payroll regulations, including tax filings and year-end activities (e.g., W-2s).

  • Perform regular payroll audits to identify discrepancies and ensure accuracy.

  • Assist in preparing payroll reports and supporting documentation as needed.

  • Respond to employee payroll inquiries and provide timely resolution.

  • Reconcile payroll registers to each pay period, Validate hours; resolve variances promptly

  • Collaborate with HR, Finance, and other teams to ensure accurate employee data and payroll processing.

  • Perform pre  and post-payroll audits each cycle to catch errors before disbursement.

  • Support internal/external audit engagements and SOX compliance; maintain payroll internal controls documentation.

  • Identify process gaps and recommend improvements to strengthen accuracy and efficiency.

  • Conduct periodic internal audits for compliance with FLSA, state wage laws, and CBA provisions.

• 3–5+ years of payroll processing experience.

  • Working knowledge of payroll practices, compliance requirements, and multi-state payroll processing.

  • Experience with payroll systems such as ADP (Workforce Now or Lyric) and time & attendance systems.

  •  Advanced Excel skills (pivot tables, VLOOKUPs, data validation) for reconciliation and auditing.

  •  Working knowledge of FLSA and IRS payroll tax regulations.

  • Familiarity with payroll reporting and account reconciliations.

  • Proficiency in Google Workspace or similar tools.

  • Strong attention to detail, organizational skills, and ability to manage deadlines.

  • Effective communication and problem-solving skills.

  • Experience in a fast-paced or high-growth environment is a plus.

  • Exposure to collective bargaining agreements is preferred.

  • Associate's or Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or Business (or equivalent experience)

  • FPC/CPP designation is a plus.

In the $50 billion student mobility market – the largest segment of the mass mobility industry – Zūm CMX  is transforming a daily source of anxiety and disruption into a reliable, transparent, and efficient mobility experience for students and families. Today, more than 6,500 schools rely on Zūm CMX. Recognized globally for its innovative approach and operational execution, Zūm has been named to Fast Company’s World’s Most Innovative Companies, CNBC Disruptor 50 and Changemakers, the World Economic Forum, and the Financial Times’ Fastest Growing Companies lists. Zūm is backed by leading investors including Sequoia Capital, GIC, TPG, and Softbank.

About the Role

We're seeking an experienced Safety Manager to lead safety operations at our Howard County, MD location. This role encompasses the complete safety lifecycle—from program development and training implementation to incident management and regulatory compliance. You'll build a culture of behavioral safety, manage safety department staff, and establish best-in-class safety standards that protect employees, students, and the communities we serve. You'll be the guardian of our most important value, ensuring every person arrives home safely every day.

 

What Makes You Successful in This Role

You're a passionate safety advocate with a commitment to zero incidents. You balance proactive prevention with responsive incident management in dynamic transportation environments. You make safety training engaging and memorable, turning compliance requirements into genuine behavior change. You analyze incident data, conduct field observations with drivers, present safety metrics to district administrators, and investigate accident scenes with equal confidence. You interpret regulations, influence behavior through clear communication, and build a culture where safety is everyone's responsibility.

lists.content:
Safety Culture & Training Leadership

  • Champion behavioral safety principles throughout the organization. Design, develop, and implement comprehensive initial and recurrent training programs for all transportation personnel including drivers, monitors, and support staff.

  • Oversee all training activities including new driver training, safety training, in-service training, driver road evaluations, special education training, first aid training, and all other required training.

  • Conduct regularly scheduled safety meetings, recognition programs, and award programs that reinforce Zum's safety-first culture and meet or exceed state, federal, FMCSA, DOT, and district requirements.

    • Performance Management & Compliance

  • Utilize Zum's safety management systems to monitor, analyze, and exceed safety KPIs including accident frequency, severity rates, training compliance, and behavioral observation metrics.

  • Ensure complete compliance with FMCSA regulations, state pupil transportation laws, OSHA standards, DOT requirements, and maintain meticulous safety records, training documentation, and regulatory files ready for audit.

  • Monitor Netradyne alerts and vehicle camera systems to proactively address retraining opportunities, and maintain individual driver files including training dates and accident history.

    • Team Development & Safety Operations

  • Manage and lead safety department staff including Field Supervisors and Driver Trainers by establishing clear objectives, performance standards, work schedules, and accountability measures.

  • Collaborate with Recruiting teams to recruit, select, and maintain authorized staffing levels, coordinate drug testing requirements, and ensure all required certifications are up to date.

  • Supervise and oversee the work of Master Trainers and certified drivers/trainers who assist with general bus driver training, ensuring training delivery meets standards.

    • Incident Management & Investigation

  • Serve as primary point of contact for all personnel injuries and vehicle accidents, ensuring immediate response and proper case management.

  • Lead thorough accident and incident investigations using root cause analysis methodologies and prepare all required incident reports in accordance with Zum policy and regulatory requirements.

  • Coordinate with insurance adjusters, claims administrators, and workers' compensation providers to ensure proper documentation and timely resolution. Interface directly with customers to communicate incident details and corrective actions.

Basic Qualifications:

  • Minimum of 5 years of professional experience in safety management within the transportation industry, with a strong preference for experience in school bus or passenger transportation.

  • In-depth knowledge of FMCSA regulations, state pupil transportation laws, OSHA/DOT standards.

    •  

    Preferred Qualifications:

  • Supervisory experience, specifically in supervising and training a driver workforce.

  • Commercial Driver's License with Passenger and School Bus Endorsements.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present complex data and findings clearly.

  • Certified Safety Professional (CSP), Certified Director of Pupil Transportation (CDPT), or other relevant safety certifications are preferred.

  • SBDI (School Bus Driver Instructor) certification.

  • Prior experience with vehicle camera and monitoring systems.

Zūm is scaling its go-to-market team and looking for a Senior BDR who can do more than book a demo — we need someone who can get in front of the district and state decision-makers who matter and turn a cold name on a list into a warm, qualified conversation for our SVP of Sales, Student Transportation. You'll own top-of-funnel pipeline for a defined territory of school districts and municipal transit agencies, running sharp, informed outreach to Transportation Directors, Superintendents, and other decision-makers — and you'll be the one who knows how to get a SVP a real meeting, not just a slot on a calendar. This is a senior individual contributor role with a clear growth path as we continue to scale. 
 
Candidates considered for this role should live in the New York or Illinois area.

• Build and manage a target account list of school districts, charter authorities, and transit agencies, prioritizing by budget cycle, contract expiration, and strategic fit

  • Run high-volume, well-researched outreach to Transportation Directors, Superintendents, CFOs, and Business Officials, and Chief Operating Officers — positioning Zūm CMX and securing meaningful first meetings, not just demo slots

  • Qualify inbound and outbound leads against Zūm's ideal customer profile before handing off, so every meeting booked for the SVP or Account Executive team is a real opportunity

  • Represent Zūm at state and regional transportation conferences (e.g., NAPT, STN Expo, state pupil transportation association events), building relationships and generating warm introductions

  • Activity logging, lead scoring, GTM research, and next steps — so pipeline reporting is accurate and forecastable

  • Partner closely with Marketing on account-based campaigns and with Sales leadership to continuously refine targeting, messaging, and outreach cadence

  • Provide field intelligence back to Product and Marketing on what districts are asking for, budgeting for, and struggling with

• 5+ years of outbound business development or sales experience, ideally in K-12 EdTech, transportation, govtech, or another market selling into school districts or government/municipal buyers

  • Demonstrated track record of booking meetings with senior decision-makers (Superintendents, Transportation Directors, C-suite) 

  • Comfort and credibility engaging with public-sector buyers, including familiarity with district budget cycles, procurement basics, and board approval processes

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills; able to build a compelling, tailored case for a meeting rather than working from a single script

  • Willingness to travel to industry conferences and, periodically, into territory for in-person relationship building

  • Self-directed and resilient — thrives on ownership of a territory with limited day-to-day oversight

• Existing relationships or name recognition with K-12 School District Leaders, including but not limited to Superintendents, Chief Financial Officers (CFOs), Chief Operating Officers (COOs), Business Officials, and Transportation Directors in (IL and the Midwest and NY and the Northeast)

  • Experience selling into or alongside long, multi-stakeholder public-sector sales cycles, and RFP processes

  • Familiarity with a state pupil transportation association (e.g., TAPT, NYAPT) or attendance at NAPT/STN Expo, desired 

  • Experience partnering directly with VP/C-level sales leadership on strategic account planning

This role is based at the Company’s headquarters in Redwood Shores, CA and requires you to be onsite 3x/week (Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday). We will only consider candidates already based in the Bay Area.

Who You Are: Zūm is modernizing its iOS experience, and we're looking for a Senior iOS Engineer to help drive that work. Our iOS surface area spans multiple apps — Driver, Parent, Student, School, and Charter — that need to feel like one coherent product, moving thousands of students, vehicles, and school districts through a real-time logistics network.

You're a strong individual contributor who wants real influence over technical direction: architecture decisions, modernization strategy, and how the team approaches iOS engineering, while staying hands-on writing production code. This isn't a feature-factory role — you'll be a key voice in setting the technical bar for iOS at Zūm.

You'll work closely with our mobile lead, product, design, and engineering leadership on what the platform should look like, then help build the efforts that get us there.

What You'll Do:

  • Help own the architecture and technical roadmap for the iOS platform
  • Contribute to modernization efforts that move the codebase toward a modern, scalable, shared platform underneath multiple apps
  • Balance new feature delivery, legacy maintenance, and platform modernization work as we prepare the app for faster feature delivery
  • Partner closely with our mobile lead, product, design, and engineering leadership on technical direction, and collaborate with mobile engineering partners on shared work
  • Work across a wide surface area of APIs and services, bringing consumer-app polish to an operationally complex, enterprise-scale problem
  • Help set the technical bar for iOS at Zūm: code quality, architecture patterns, and how the team approaches modernization
  • Leverage AI tooling to accelerate development, improve code quality, and speed up modernization work
  • Modernize legacy features of the app toward current SwiftUI patterns without stalling feature delivery
  • Contribute to a shared platform layer that multiple Zūm apps (Driver, Parent, Student, School, Charter) can build on top of, instead of duplicating logic across codebases
  • Rework how the app handles a large and growing surface area of APIs so the codebase stays maintainable as complexity increases
  • Improve app performance and memory footprint, and build out telemetry/monitoring so the team can see how the app behaves in production
  • Help identify which parts of the current app are worth keeping versus updating, and execute

    • What You Bring To Zūm:

  • 5+ years of professional iOS engineering experience, with real depth
  • Strong, current command of Swift and SwiftUI; you're living in modern iOS development
  • Experience owning meaningful parts of a consumer-facing app end-to-end, not just a single feature, page, or internal tool
  • A product-first orientation: comfortable with infrastructure work, but your track record is primarily product-driven
  • Experience working in a complex, consumer-facing app environment (think feature-rich apps with a large user base vs. a narrow enterprise tool or an SDK)
  • Comfort contributing to architectural decisions and modernization efforts at scale
  • Experience modernizing a legacy iOS app while it's still shipping features (preferred)
  • Background at a company with a small-to-mid-sized mobile team, where you had real hands-on ownership (preferred)
  • Experience partnering with an engineering leader or mobile lead on setting technical direction (preferred)

    • Bonus Points:

  • Domain experience in logistics, mapping, or fleet-style products
  • Experience working across multiple related apps sharing common infrastructure or design systems

If you are a full-time salaried or hourly worker, we offer the following benefits: Medical, Dental, Vision, 401(k), Holidays, Wellness, Vacation, and more. You care about shipping features that customers actually feel, and you measure your work by the business outcomes it drives.
You want to build customer-facing product functionality on top of Zūm's platform, moving fast without cutting corners.
You're self-driven, enjoy solving ambiguous product problems, and default to the simplest solution that meets the need.
You partner easily with Product and Design, and you take full ownership of what you ship, from spec to production.

Own one or more product verticals within backend engineering, building customer-facing features end-to-end.

Write high-quality, maintainable, testable code, and participate actively in code review.
Instrument what you build for visibility and traceability using tools like Datadog, Rollbar, and Segment.

Bachelor's degree or higher in Computer Science or equivalent experience.
5+ years of industry experience as a Software Engineer, ideally with experience building product features on top of a shared backend platform.
Excellence in one or more backend languages: Node.js, Java, or Python, with strong TypeScript/Node.js preferred.
Experience working with relational and non-relational databases.
Hands-on experience deploying and managing applications on the cloud (AWS/Google Cloud).
Good planning, organization, and decision-making skills.
Strong communication with engineers, product managers, and other stakeholders.
Good sense of humor with a great ability to work with others.

Passionate about working for a mission-driven company.

descriptionBody:
This role is based at the Company's headquarters in Redwood Shores, CA and requires you to be onsite 3x/week (Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday). We will only consider candidates already based in the Bay Area.

Who You Are:

  • You care about shipping features that customers actually feel, and you measure your work by the business outcomes it drives.
  • You want to build customer-facing product functionality on top of Zūm's platform, moving fast without cutting corners.
  • You're self-driven, enjoy solving ambiguous product problems, and default to the simplest solution that meets the need.
  • You partner easily with Product and Design, and you take full ownership of what you ship, from spec to production.

What You'll Do:

  • Own one or more product verticals within backend engineering, building customer-facing features end-to-end.
  • Build microservices and APIs using our stack: Kubernetes, Kafka, PostgreSQL, gRPC, and related tools consuming the platform primitives (auth, data access, shared services) our platform team provides rather than building them yourself.
  • Work closely with Product and Design to translate requirements into technical designs and shipped functionality.
  • Write high-quality, maintainable, testable code, and participate actively in code review.
  • Instrument what you build for visibility and traceability using tools like Datadog, Rollbar, and Segment.
  • Contribute to engineering practices within your team, but the platform's shared standards and infrastructure are owned by the Platform Infrastructure team, not you.

What You Bring To Zūm:

  • Bachelor's degree or higher in Computer Science or equivalent experience.
  • 5+ years of industry experience as a Software Engineer, ideally with experience building product features on top of a shared backend platform.
  • Excellence in one or more backend languages: Node.js, Java, or Python, with strong TypeScript/Node.js preferred.
  • Experience working with relational and non-relational databases.
  • Hands-on experience deploying and managing applications on the cloud (AWS/Google Cloud).
  • Good planning, organization, and decision-making skills.
  • Strong communication with engineers, product managers, and other stakeholders.
  • Good sense of humor with a great ability to work with others.

Bonus Points:

  • Passionate about working for a mission-driven company.
  • Experience working in the transportation industry.
  • Strong experience with Node.js and TypeScript.

The targeted base salary range for this role is listed in the compensation section below. Actual salary may be above or below this range based on factors such as location, skills, and relevant experience. In addition, this position may include additional compensation in the form of equity or commissions. If you are a full-time salaried or hourly worker, we offer the following benefits: Medical, Dental, Vision, 401(k), Holidays, Wellness, Vacation, and more. The targeted pay range for this role in CA, USA is: $190,000 - $260,000 plus stock options.
